Tulane Green Wave.previous_hc_experience: Yes, and the guide treats it as the central issue. The Coaching Carousel records that Will Hall had a miserable tenure at Southern Miss, going 14-30 over three seasons and seven games, that he went to Hattiesburg after serving as Tulane's OC in 2019-20, and that he was a fairly hot commodity after some strong seasons at West Alabama and West Georgia as a young head coach before his star faded.
Tulane Green Wave.oc: Not addressed in guide. Hall was Tulane's pass game coordinator before the promotion.
Tulane Green Wave.dc: Tayler Polk, promoted from co-coordinator to full coordinator.
Tulane Green Wave.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Tulane Green Wave.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator, and the guide records Polk's promotion from co-coordinator.
Tulane Green Wave.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Tulane Green Wave.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Tulane Green Wave.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the unit struggling against the pass, allowing 262 yards per game and a 67.6% completion rate.
Tulane Green Wave.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Tulane Green Wave.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide is dryly candid about the room, noting Zeon Chriss-Gremillion has played a very long time in college with a hyphenated name the most notable development, and that Kadin Semonza redshirted without playing after starting at Ball State.
Tulane Green Wave.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback all change; the defensive coordinator returns. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 0, 0, 3 and 0, plus 1 for 8 returning starters, totalling 4.
Tulane Green Wave.staff_turnover: Substantial, following Jon Sumrall's departure, with the head coach promoted internally from pass game coordinator and the defensive coordinator promoted from co-coordinator.
Tulane Green Wave.prior_school: Tulane itself for Hall, who has had two stints there including as offensive coordinator in 2019-20. Southern Miss, West Alabama and West Georgia are his head-coaching reference points. The guide notes Sumrall inherited a strong foundation and brought talent from Troy, a luxury Hall may not have.
Tulane Green Wave.portal_recruiting: Rated weak relative to the programme's standing. Tulane's portal class ranks seventh among 14 American teams, which the guide calls unimpressive for a programme with three 11-win seasons and a 9-5 campaign in four years. It credits the Polk promotion with possibly retaining leading tacklers Jack Tchienchou and Chris Rodgers.
Tulane Green Wave.vsin_assessment: Disappointed in the process, then partially self-correcting on the man. The Coaching Carousel says losing Willie Fritz and then Jon Sumrall would be tough for any programme, but that not taking a third swing at a rising name feels like a miss, and concludes it just feels like the Green Wave took the easy route, which seems really disappointing. The team pages revise their own view openly: Hall has had two stints at Tulane and success at West Alabama and West Georgia, so he may deserve more benefit of the doubt than his messy Southern Miss tenure — which included a conference change — had earned him. Elsewhere they are harsher, calling him an awful head coach at Southern Miss without nearly the offensive upside of last year's squad.
Tulane Green Wave.strengths: A defensive coordinator promoted internally with retention of the two leading tacklers credited to it, prior familiarity with the programme from two earlier stints, and a documented record of success at West Alabama and West Georgia.
Tulane Green Wave.concerns: A 14-30 head-coaching record at his last FBS stop, an 11-3 season the guide says was built on a +24 sack differential, four wins while being outgained and five by one score; the loss of the quarterback, leading receiver and much of the production; a portal class ranked seventh in the conference; and a pass defense allowing 262 yards per game.
Tulane Green Wave.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its coaching-linked conclusion is that it feels like the 2025 result could come crashing down on Hall, with a projection of 7.56 wins.
Tulane Green Wave.carousel_summary: Adam Burke's objection is to the search rather than only the man: losing Willie Fritz and then Jon Sumrall would be tough for any programme, but not taking a third swing at a rising name feels like a miss. Instead, he writes, Tulane promoted pass game coordinator Will Hall, who had a miserable tenure at Southern Miss, going 14-30 over three seasons and seven games. He gives the fuller arc — Hall went to Hattiesburg after serving as Tulane's OC in 2019-20 and was a fairly hot commodity after some strong seasons at West Alabama and West Georgia as a young head coach, but his star faded after the Southern Miss years. His verdict: it just feels like the Green Wave took the easy route, and that seems really disappointing.

Tulsa Golden Hurricane.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed as head-coaching experience. The guide records that the 36-year-old Tre Lamb was a quarterback at Tennessee Tech then its coordinator, and calls him a rapid riser.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.dc: Josh Reardon, entering year two of his scheme.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.oc_status: The guide states this two ways — see the conflicts field. The team pages (pp. 72–73) call Kevin Barbay the new coordinator, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.dc_status: Returning — the guide records year two of Josh Reardon's scheme, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide expects heavy running with more designed runs for Baylor Hayes, and notes nearly 500 rushing attempts last season with an even higher figure expected.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records year two of Reardon's scheme featuring both players who know it and transfers who are likely better fits.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.run_pass: Run-weighted and increasing — nearly 500 rushing attempts last season, with the guide expecting more, and describing the offensive line as built for it.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.personnel: Addressed through the offensive line: the guide notes every starter and two-deep player is at or above 300 pounds, which it reads as exactly what Lamb wants.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Baylor Hayes staying — which it says could make a major difference despite an entirely new skill group — and gives the full sequence of his season rather than only the highlight, noting the upset of Oklahoma State was followed by three straight blowout losses before Tulsa was largely competitive against comparable or lesser opponents.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.continuity: The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4 for the head coach, 3 for the offensive coordinator, 3 for the defensive coordinator and 4 for the quarterback, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 15. The team pages describe the offensive coordinator position differently — see the conflicts field.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.staff_turnover: The team pages record Kevin Barbay arriving as coordinator.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.prior_school: Tennessee Tech is Lamb's own background. On the roster the guide records offensive line transfers from Texas A&M and Ole Miss brought in last season, South Alabama's starting center Malachi Preciado who was originally at Purdue, and productive running back transfers from Auburn and Old Dominion.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.portal_recruiting: Framed as a virtuous circle by the guide: with the programme showing more stability, transfers are now more willing to come.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.vsin_assessment: Direction credited over record. The guide says Tulsa looked better without the record following at 4-8 and judges Lamb's team is moving in the right direction, establishing the baseline being improved from — arguably the nation's worst defense in 2024 at 42.5 points and 7.1 yards per play allowed — and recording gains of nearly 14 fewer points and 1.5 fewer yards per play allowed. Its open question is whether Lamb and Barbay can inject life into the offense.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.strengths: A documented defensive turnaround from arguably the nation's worst unit, a retained quarterback, a Stability Score of 15, a heavily rebuilt offensive line where every starter and two-deep player is 300-plus pounds, year two of the defensive scheme, and top defensive backs returning.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.concerns: An offense that made few strides, the loss of a 1,000-yard rusher and the top three pass catchers, 11 takeaways for a -9 turnover margin, and the top two tacklers gone.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
Tulsa Golden Hurricane.conflicts: The guide states the offensive coordinator position two ways. The team pages (pp. 72–73) refer to new coordinator Kevin Barbay and ask whether he and Tre Lamb can inject life into the offense, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator. Both are reproduced as printed and neither is corrected.

UAB Blazers.previous_hc_experience: Only at UAB itself, and the Coaching Carousel is precise about it: Mortensen isn't a new head coach, per se, as he took over when Trent Dilfer was booted from Birmingham, but he's the full-time man now, and he was 2-4 in his six games.
UAB Blazers.oc: Alex Mortensen himself — he was coordinator when promoted, kept calling plays as interim and will continue while overseeing the whole programme.
UAB Blazers.dc: Todd Grantham, a veteran who has coached at premier college programmes and in the NFL, replacing Steve Russ.
UAB Blazers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator, consistent with Mortensen keeping the role himself.
UAB Blazers.dc_status: New — the guide records Grantham's hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
UAB Blazers.play_caller: Alex Mortensen on offense, explicitly, and the guide asks whether he should be — finding a mitigating factor in Grantham, who has been around long enough not to need supervision.
UAB Blazers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide notes little changed for the offense late in the season beyond running more often, even in blowout losses to UConn, North Texas and South Florida.
UAB Blazers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, though the guide calls Grantham's possibly complex. It makes a specific point about the outgoing coordinator's background — plotting a defense for a triple-option team is very different from Birmingham — and notes UAB was unsurprisingly better against the run under Steve Russ while conceding many more explosive pass plays.
UAB Blazers.run_pass: The guide expects the pass game to become less important, and builds a game-state argument on it: because of that, it worries UAB projects to trail often.
UAB Blazers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Ryder Burton, who arrived via BYU and West Virginia, as at least a starting point.
UAB Blazers.continuity: The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4 for the head coach, 3 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 4 returning starters, totalling 7. Virtually everybody on defense and most of the offense is gone.
UAB Blazers.staff_turnover: Extensive at coordinator over a short period. The guide reviews it: Steve Russ and Sione Ta'ufo'ou were coordinators under Dilfer, Ta'ufo'ou returned to Cal and Russ came from Air Force, with Grantham now in place.
UAB Blazers.prior_school: Air Force and Cal are where the previous coordinators came from and went. Oklahoma State is Grantham's most recent stop. On the roster the guide records Ryder Burton via BYU and West Virginia, Rod Robinson from Georgia and Bam McReynolds from ULM.
UAB Blazers.portal_recruiting: The whole roster, and the guide is frank about its quality: portal additions from all over make up the defense and most of the offense, many of them multi-time transfers who have not latched on anywhere, including a patchwork line, and nobody on the two-deep is proven.
UAB Blazers.vsin_assessment: Two readings of the same promotion, and the guide keeps both. The Coaching Carousel says simply elevating Mortensen from OC reeks of being too cheap to make an impact hire, notes the upset of Memphis in his first game may very well have been the deciding factor in keeping him, and recalls that the Dilfer hire was out of left field when the players desperately wanted Bryant Vincent. The team pages agree on the motive — a penny-pinching athletic director — but rate the defensive hire highly, calling Grantham the best coordinator UAB has had in a long time and using salary as evidence of institutional commitment: Grantham earned $1.3 million at Oklahoma State before being fired four games in, while Mortensen makes $1 million, so bringing him in is a large investment that says something.
UAB Blazers.strengths: A defensive coordinator the guide calls the best UAB has had in a long time, with premier college and NFL experience and a salary the guide reads as genuine institutional commitment; a head coach with a signature upset already; and a blank slate the guide says is as blank as possible.
UAB Blazers.concerns: A promotion both parts of the guide attribute to cost-saving, a head coach also calling his own offense while running the whole programme, one returning player with more than 20 tackles, a roster largely of multi-time transfers who have not latched on anywhere, a patchwork offensive line, and a game-state problem the guide expects — trailing often.
UAB Blazers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Projection is 3.63 wins.
UAB Blazers.carousel_summary: Adam Burke starts by clarifying the status: Mortensen isn't a new head coach, per se, as he took over when Trent Dilfer was booted from Birmingham, but he's the full-time man now. He records the audition — 2-4 in his six games, with a big upset of Memphis in his first game at the helm, which may very well have been the deciding factor in just keeping him. He then reaches back for the pattern: the Dilfer hire was out of left field, to say the least, when the players desperately wanted Bryant Vincent to take over the job permanently after he filled in for Bill Clark, but that didn't happen. His verdict on the sequel is blunt — simply elevating Mortensen from OC reeks of being too cheap to make an impact hire.

UTSA Roadrunners.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Jeff Traylor in his seventh season and notes he is the only head coach in the conference whose tenure approaches Jeff Monken's.
UTSA Roadrunners.oc: Rick Bowie, in after Western Kentucky last season, Abilene Christian in 2024 and Valdosta State in 2022-23.
UTSA Roadrunners.dc: Jess Loepp, in the role since 2020.
UTSA Roadrunners.oc_status: New — the guide calls Bowie a very intriguing fit as new coordinator, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
UTSA Roadrunners.dc_status: Returning — Loepp has held the role since 2020, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
UTSA Roadrunners.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
UTSA Roadrunners.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but characterised by the coordinator's history: the guide records Bowie having led prolific passing offenses and expects him to unlock more from Owen McCown.
UTSA Roadrunners.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's plan note is that UTSA intends to rotate linemen and keep fresh rushers on the field.
UTSA Roadrunners.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split beyond the coordinator's passing background.
UTSA Roadrunners.personnel: Addressed through the stated rotation of defensive linemen.
UTSA Roadrunners.qb_development: Addressed as an expectation attached to the new coordinator. The guide ties UTSA's ceiling to Owen McCown, records him falling just short of 3,000 passing yards with 30 touchdown passes, notes he retains rapport with David Amador and AJ Wilson, and expects Bowie to unlock more.
UTSA Roadrunners.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 1 for 8 returning starters, totalling 12.
UTSA Roadrunners.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive coordinator, though the guide raises the possibility of more: it wonders openly whether Jess Loepp, in the role since 2020, makes it through the season.
UTSA Roadrunners.prior_school: Western Kentucky, Abilene Christian and Valdosta State for Bowie. The guide also records former UTSA pass rushers leaving upward — Jimmori Robinson to West Virginia and Trey Moore finishing at Texas — and top receiver Devin McCuin being taken by Ohio State, noting drily that they know something about receivers.
UTSA Roadrunners.portal_recruiting: Substantial in volume, weak in ranking, and structurally explained. Per 247Sports UTSA brought in 21 transfers, 12 on defense, though its class ranks 11th of the 12 American teams with portal access — so the guide reserves judgement on whether the right pieces were bought. It explains the structural cause of the pass-rush problem: Group of Six players who can reach the quarterback are the most sought-after by schools with bigger NIL budgets.
UTSA Roadrunners.vsin_assessment: A long tenure with one persistent failing named directly. The guide calls this one of the American's most experienced offenses with Rick Bowie a very intriguing fit, flags that the defense must improve and wonders whether Loepp makes it through the season, then catalogues the pattern that defines its reservation: losses to Temple and Army as a favorite last season plus a non-conference loss as favorite to Texas State, and losses to Rice and Tulsa in favorite roles in 2024, with UTSA not even reaching the conference title game. Its conclusion is conditional — that should change with this schedule, but Traylor must take care of business when expected to, something he has struggled with.
UTSA Roadrunners.strengths: One of the conference's longest-tenured head coaches with Conference USA titles in 2021 and 2022, one of the American's most experienced offenses, a returning quarterback approaching programme passing records, a coordinator hire the guide calls very intriguing with a record of prolific passing offenses, defensive-coordinator continuity since 2020, and a deliberate portal focus on pass rushers with much stronger depth.
UTSA Roadrunners.concerns: A pass rush that fell from 46 and 42 sacks to 24, a portal class ranked 11th of 12, a defense the guide says must improve with its coordinator's job in question, and a documented pattern of losing as a favorite.
UTSA Roadrunners.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching, though its coaching-linked conclusion is stated in market terms: Traylor must take care of business when expected to, something he has struggled with.
